raw_signal: (no owner signal -- this came out of a macro pass)
observations: After a reveal, a plain reload of `/play` returns the same board -- square-by-square aria-label signature identical -- with `.reveal-panel` absent and `.commitment-submit` reading `חסר: בחרו מהלך על הלוח`. The screen is re-armed for a decision on a position that has already been decided.

Deciding again is accepted with no error. Measured: `decision-lab.record.v1.decisions` went from 3 rows to 4, two carrying an identical FEN, both `purpose: "anchor"`, and the reveal's verdict sentence for the second was byte-identical to the first.
Two other routes reach the same screen: browser Back from `/`, and the brand lockup out to `/` followed by the `ללוח` control back.

The cause is a split of state: `session-position.ts` persists the position so a reload does not lose the game, and the reveal is component state, so the reload keeps the position and drops the only thing that said it had been decided.

The product enforces the opposite rule in three other places. `shared/drill-positions.ts`: a drill is a forward test, keyed by board on both sides so a position already answered cannot enter. `shared/record-service.ts` on the transfer resume: 'a returning player was served a board they had already decided and seen the engine's verdict for ... re-serving a decided position is the thing per-position writes were introduced to prevent'. And `preregisterFreshTransfer`: novelty is a property of the board, not of the FEN string.
On screen the two numbers disagree and neither is wrong: `הסט המשותף · 3 מתוך 60 עמדות` beside `4 החלטות שלכם נרשמו`. Progress dedupes by position id; the record counts rows.

candidate_mechanisms.name: The reload is a resume and re-arming is correct; the second decision is a real decision
candidate_mechanisms.explains: Why `session-position.ts` exists at all, and why the board deliberately does not advance after a reveal.
candidate_mechanisms.does_not_explain: That the player has already been shown the engine's verdict for that position, which is the condition the drill and transfer paths refuse by name.

candidate_mechanisms.name: The re-arm is an omission: the loop never reconciles the persisted position with the decided-ness the record already knows
candidate_mechanisms.explains: Everything measured, and why the three other consumers enforce the rule and this one does not.
candidate_mechanisms.discriminator: OWNER for what the screen should do instead. The reading half is already repaired and does not wait on it.

design_distinction: A resume restores what you were doing. It is not the same act as re-asking a question you have already been given the answer to, and one screen was doing both because the two halves of its state have different lifetimes.
authority: REPO for the reachability, the record rows and the disagreement between the two numbers, all measured. OWNER for what a re-armed board should do.
intervention: PARTIAL, AND ONLY ON THE READING. The between-player comparison now admits one answer per bank position, keeping the first -- the only one the record can place before any verdict on that position existed. That closes the measurement half without deciding the screen half.
must_not_change: `anchorAnswered`. It decides which position the front door serves next, and narrowing it would re-serve a position the player has already answered -- the same defect arriving from the other direction. A positive control holds it.
perceptual_success_criterion: A player who reloads after a reveal is not asked for a decision they have already given, or is told that is what they are being asked for.
check: `tests/shared/a-bank-position-answered-twice.test.ts` holds the reading half, with the free-play population and the front door's progress both held un-deduped as positive controls.
next_step: One decision from the owner: on a reload onto a decided position, does the screen refuse, advance to the next position, or say plainly that this one has been answered and offer both? Each is a different sentence and a different claim about what a resume is.
